To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the incidences of focal hyperplasia and/or adenoma in the pancreas of male F344/N Nctr rats were significantly increased in 2 of 5 studies, and in 1 of 2 studies in which corn oil was administered by gavage, but not when corn oil was administered in the diet.

focal acinar hyperpla- sia and acinar adenomas of the pancreas are common in male rats of NCI/NTP toxicology studies in which the vehicle is corn oil administered by gavage and that the lesions are not associated with the test chemical.

(1) the incidence of acinar hyperlasias, adenomas, and carcinomas was increased in rats given corn oil gavage, (2) corn oil induced acinar hyperplasias, adenomas and carcinomas were not associated with inflammation, (3) corn oil induced lesions were not associated with pancreatic atrophy, and (4) the presence of corn oil in the lumen of the pancreas was associated with focal acinar hyperlasia.
In summary, our research is concerned with
understanding the biology of pancreatic acinar lesions in the rat and with developing methods for assessing the significance of the lesions.
the study of the biological behavior and etiology of proliferative lesions in the rat pancreas.
the development of new, more effective methods of treatment for pancreatic cancer.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
corn oil gavage induces focal acinar hyperlasia in male F344 rats.
acinar adenoma and carcinoma are considered to be a continuum and are considered to be preneoplastic lesions.
the test chemical was not a carcinogen to male rats.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the rat is a sensitive species for the detection of pancreatic carcinogens.
we have shown that the exocrine pancreata of F344 male rats are susceptible to the development of focal acinar lesions.
the rat pancreas can be a sensitive target for the induction of pancreatic cancer.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the rat pancreas has a remarkable ability to respond to injury by proliferative lesions of various degrees of severity and that these lesions are not always associated with carcinogenicity.
the rat pancreas, like the mouse, is a sensitive target for the development of pancreatic neoplasia.
corn oil gavage causes a high incidence of focal acinar cell hyperplasia and a lower incidence of acinar cell adenoma.
